title: Iki compute template (iki/v1)
description: A kind of machine a deployment runs actions on: how it starts, its size, where it runs and what it costs. Compute admins keep templates in the deployment's config repository, in compute.yaml.

provisioner.description: How machines start. `backend_pool`: Iki's backend worker pods (backend tier). `k8s_job`: a Kubernetes Job for each run, and `k8s_deployment`: a warm pool of pods (container tier). `aws_ec2`: EC2 instances (vm tier).

lifecycle.description: For `aws_ec2`: a machine for each run (`ephemeral`, the default), or warm machines that shut down when idle (`persistent`).

capacity.description: What each machine gives a run. A job runs here only if it fits.

kubernetes.description: For the Kubernetes provisioners: where pods are scheduled.

runtime_class.description: A RuntimeClass for stronger isolation, such as `gvisor` or `kata`.

aws.description: For `aws_ec2`: the instances and where they start.

image.description: The machine image instances boot: an AMI ID, or `resolve:ssm:` and a Systems Manager parameter that holds one, such as AWS's ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2023 (`resolve:ssm:/aws/service/ecs/optimized-ami/amazon-linux-2023/recommended/image_id`, or `.../amazon-linux-2023/gpu/recommended/image_id` for GPUs). It needs Docker, and for GPUs NVIDIA's drivers and container toolkit.

spot.description: Use spot instances, which cost less but can be taken back with two minutes' notice.

fallback.description: With `spot`: start an on-demand instance when no spot capacity is free (`on_demand`), or wait (`none`, the default).

subnets.description: Private subnets, one or more for each zone runs may use.

security_groups.description: Security groups for the instances: none needs inbound rules, and outbound only to Iki, object storage, the egress proxy and the image registry.

instance_profile.description: The IAM instance profile workers start with. It needs no permissions beyond reaching Iki.

root_device.description: The image's root device, which gets the disk: `/dev/xvda` (Amazon Linux, the default) or `/dev/sda1` (Ubuntu, say).

root_disk.description: The size of each instance's disk, encrypted and deleted with it. Unless set, `capacity.scratch_disk` and 40Gi for the image and the system.

kms_key.description: The KMS key that encrypts the disks, by ARN or alias; the account's default EBS key unless set.

tags.description: More tags for the instances and their disks, such as a cost center. Iki's own tags (`iki.ikisci.org/…`) and AWS's (`aws:…`) are taken.

volumes.description: How machines get each environment volume, by the volume's name.

strategy.description: `clone_from_snapshot`: a new disk from the volume's snapshot for each machine. `attach_exclusive`: one disk, attached to one machine at a time. `shared_filesystem`: a network file system many machines mount. `object_mount`: the data in object storage, mounted read-only.

fast_snapshot_restore.description: With `clone_from_snapshot` on AWS: disks start at full speed, at extra cost.

storage_class.description: On Kubernetes: the StorageClass of the disks made for the volume (the cluster's default unless set).

snapshot_class.description: On Kubernetes, with `clone_from_snapshot`: the VolumeSnapshotClass its snapshots are taken with (the cluster's default unless set).

max_concurrent.description: The most machines (or pods) running at once.

min_warm.description: For persistent machines: how many to keep running when idle.

idle_shutdown.description: For persistent machines: how long one waits for work before it stops.

price.description: What a machine costs while it runs, for cost records and budgets.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as `USD` or `EUR`.
